question: Do autoregressive Transformers deliberately compute features at an earlier token because those features will help predict later tokens, or are useful earlier states merely reusable breadcrumbs?

key_findings.claim: Myopic training removes off-diagonal gradient contributions from future-token losses to parameters as used at a past position, eliminating the direct training incentive to pre-cache future-useful features.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3 decomposes the ordinary autoregressive gradient and defines tied and untied myopia. The custom attention backward pass stops gradients through cached past key/value states while retaining their forward use.

anchors.section: Section 3.2-3.3, gradient decomposition and myopia gap

key_findings.claim: A constructed task that rewards computing sin(bx) before it becomes relevant yields strong direct evidence of learned pre-caching under ordinary training.
key_findings.evidence: Linear probes recover sin(bx_n) from vanilla hidden states at its source position, and normalized Huber loss ranges from 0.0030 to 0.096 versus 0.97 to 1.26 for myopic models across p values; an always-zero predictor scores 1.26.

key_findings.claim: On one-epoch GPT-2-small training over 4.6M MS MARCO sequences, the myopia gap is modest: validation cross-entropy is 3.40 myopic versus 3.28 vanilla, while a context-disabled Transformer bigram scores 5.33.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 also reports 3.26 for a local-myopic model supplied frozen vanilla past states. The much larger bigram gap shows that myopic models still exploit useful past breadcrumbs even without future-directed gradients.

key_findings.claim: The natural-language myopia gap increases with Pythia model size from 70M through 2.8B parameters, but these runs fine-tune pretrained checkpoints and do not isolate where pre-caching arose during original pretraining.
key_findings.evidence: Section 5.2 starts from released pretrained Pythia models because the 10M-sequence corpus is too small for scratch training; Appendix Figure 7 shows a growing post-fine-tuning vanilla-myopic loss gap.

key_findings.claim: A training-procedure gap is evidence about the benefit of pre-caching but is not a causal localization of what a particular vanilla network computes at each token.
key_findings.evidence: The authors distinguish the global myopia gap from a local-myopia bonus for a fixed model. The local bonus is only 0.02 in GPT-2, and alternative optimization effects or reduced gradient credit assignment can contribute to performance differences.

method.core_idea: Intervene on temporal credit assignment during training and use the performance loss as an operational measure of computation performed early specifically for later predictions.
method.mechanism: Decompose autoregressive gradients by source and target token, stop future losses from updating earlier cached states, compare vanilla and myopic optima or training runs, and supplement behavior with hidden-state probes and gradient-component measurements.
assumptions: Removing off-diagonal gradients selectively removes deliberate pre-caching without introducing dominant unrelated optimization costs.
Matched vanilla and myopic training reach sufficiently comparable solutions.
Cross-entropy gaps and probes reflect reusable computation rather than only capacity or convergence differences.

techniques.role: Removes future-token learning signals from earlier forward passes.
Quantifies the best-achievable or empirical value of pre-caching.
Tests the immediate-token tradeoff while holding past vanilla states fixed.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer Transformers on synthetic D_p sequences
evaluations.metric: Normalized Huber loss and probe R-squared
evaluations.result: Vanilla training learns probe-visible future-useful sine features and achieves 0.0030-0.096 loss, while myopic training remains near 0.97-1.26.
evaluations.baseline: Myopic training and an always-zero predictor

evaluations.setting: GPT-2-small trained one epoch on 4.6M length-64 MS MARCO sequences
evaluations.result: Vanilla 3.28, myopic 3.40, local-myopic 3.26, and Transformer bigram 5.33; natural language is dominated by reusable breadcrumbs at this scale.
evaluations.baseline: Myopic, local-myopic, and context-disabled matched architectures

evaluations.setting: Pretrained Pythia checkpoints from 14M to 2.8B fine-tuned on 10M Pile sequences
evaluations.result: The vanilla-myopic gap generally increases from 70M upward, suggesting greater pre-caching benefit with scale.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic multiplication with filler zero padding
evaluations.result: Longer filler padding improves vanilla models but hurts myopic models, consistent with vanilla computation occurring during otherwise meaningless tokens.

limitations: Myopic and vanilla training can differ in optimization quality for reasons besides pre-caching.
The natural-language scratch-training experiment is limited to GPT-2-small, one epoch, and length 64.
Larger Pythia experiments begin from already pretrained checkpoints.
The convergence theorem assumes smoothness and strong convexity conditions that do not describe deep Transformer training.
The study measures aggregate benefit, not a complete causal circuit for natural-language pre-caching.
failure_modes: Gradient stopping may make credit assignment harder even when no useful feature needs pre-caching.
A model can encode future-useful information incidentally, making probe decodability insufficient evidence of deliberate planning.
Pretraining can already install cached features that survive nominally myopic fine-tuning.
Sequence or dataset shifts can change the apparent myopia gap independently of planning.
reusable_insights: Separate features useful now and later from features computed now only for later by intervening on temporal gradients.
Use global performance gaps, fixed-model local bonuses, probes, and causal ablations together rather than treating any one as definitive planning evidence.
Audit filler-token computation because extra forward passes can provide hidden compute unrelated to token semantics.
open_questions: Does pre-caching remain small when frontier models are trained myopically from initialization at full corpus scale?
Which natural-language circuits and token types account causally for the size-dependent myopia gap?
Can adaptive local myopia improve interpretability or safety without sacrificing useful future computation?

competitive_landscape.title: Let's Think Dot by Dot: Hidden Computation in Transformer Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Computation on semantically empty filler tokens
competitive_landscape.difference: Pfau et al. show extra tokens can supply hidden inference compute; this paper asks whether ordinary training prepares earlier hidden states for later tokens and disables that incentive with myopic gradients.

competitive_landscape.title: Think Before You Speak: Training Language Models With Pause Tokens
competitive_landscape.difference: Pause-token training deliberately adds compute before outputs; the reviewed work diagnoses computation embedded in ordinary past-token states without adding special tokens.

competitive_landscape.title: Quiet-STaR: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Think Before Speaking
competitive_landscape.difference: Quiet-STaR explicitly trains token-level hidden rationales to improve future text; myopic training removes future-directed gradients to estimate how much analogous implicit preparation standard models learn naturally.

competitive_landscape.title: Why Can GPT Learn In-Context? Language Models Secretly Perform Gradient Descent as Meta-Optimizers
competitive_landscape.relationship: Interpretation of computation stored in Transformer states
competitive_landscape.difference: The meta-optimizer account characterizes an in-context computation; this paper focuses on when training causes an earlier position to compute information for later forward passes and provides a gradient intervention.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Myopic training operationalizes and measures Transformer pre-caching, showing it clearly in a controlled task but finding breadcrumbs more explanatory for small language models, with pre-caching increasing at scale.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies definitions, a synthetic separation with probes, matched GPT-2 runs, Pythia scaling, multiplication filler tests, and gradient decomposition.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The temporal-gradient intervention is an important diagnostic. Strong claims about model planning should remain qualified because optimization gaps and inherited pretrained features are not themselves causal circuit evidence.
